evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the stakeholder need (create a game with name/description) without prescribing concrete UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Unnecessarily prescribes a technical mechanism (sharing a URL) rather than just the need to invite estimators.

evaluations.evidence: entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete UI widget (a single multi-line text field) instead of stating the stakeholder need.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: States the need to view items without prescribing a solution or UI control.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user's goal (select an item) without specifying implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the stakeholder need to add items; does not prescribe UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the need to edit items without dictating how editing must be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: States the requirement to remove items; no concrete implementation or UI widget is prescribed.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Describes desired behavior (immediate showing) without prescribing UI controls or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a stakeholder decision (use the average) rather than a low-level implementation detail or algorithmic method.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete UI element ('estimate' field) and automatic behavior (auto-fill), which are implementation choices.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user's task without prescribing UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need to re-estimate, not a solution detail.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete technical mechanism/format (spreadsheet) instead of the general need to bulk-import stories.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific mechanism (copy/paste from spreadsheet) rather than stating the need to get stories in quickly.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user's need to find past games without mandating implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: States the desire to view transcripts; does not prescribe formats or UI widgets.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete export format (HTML), a technical/implementation choice.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete file format (CSV) instead of just the need to export for further processing.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Describes the outcome (removal of stored data) without prescribing the implementation.

evaluations.evidence: create an account ... by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Specifies required account information rather than low-level technical or UI implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: States the expected authentication method (credentials) as a functional requirement rather than prescribing low-level implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the user's need to update account details without imposing solution choices.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Specifies desired effect (data removal) without prescribing implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: States a display preference (local timezone) without mandating technical implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific technical mechanism/channel (email) for password reminders rather than the general need to recover access.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Specifies allowed estimation scales (domain choices) rather than low-level UI or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: States a capacity constraint, which is a stakeholder requirement, not an implementation choice.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Specifies joining via a URL and entering name on a page—concrete mechanism/flow rather than only the stakeholder need.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: States the need to view the item without prescribing UI widgets or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user's informational need, not a concrete solution.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the desired visibility of estimates without mandating a UI widget or implementation.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a behavioral requirement (simultaneous reveal) rather than specifying UI widgets or technical details.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Uses domain concept 'card' but specifies the user capability/condition rather than prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the information need without specifying UI or storage mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: States the requirement to attribute estimates; not a prescription of implementation.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a desired shared timing behavior (timer and duration) as a user need rather than a low-level technical solution.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Describes required timer behavior; although specific, it defines user-facing behavior rather than internal implementation.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: States the ability to navigate history without prescribing UI controls or implementation.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a consistent ordering requirement (user-facing behavior) rather than a technical implementation choice.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the user's capability without prescribing concrete UI widgets or technical details.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete UI element and placement (thumbnail displayed near cards), which is an implementation/UI decision.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete technical standards (XHTML/CSS) for implementation rather than only the stakeholder accessibility need.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: States a documentation need without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific implementation technique (database indexes) rather than expressing the need for acceptable performance.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete legacy browser versions to support (implementation/platform constraint) instead of higher-level compatibility goals.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific standard (W3C guidelines) as an implementation choice instead of stating the accessibility need more generally.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: States a performance expectation (user need) without prescribing technical implementation or specific metrics.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete technical solution/format (Unicode) rather than only the stakeholder need to use any language.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific, technical user-visible format (URL structure) rather than stating a more general navigational/transparency need.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user's expectation for friendly errors without mandating technical or UI implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a privacy requirement (non-identifiable storage) without prescribing the technical anonymization mechanism or storage format.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need for usage metrics without prescribing specific storage, algorithms, or UI details.
